# QA-001 Supplier Quality / NCR Procedure

## 1. Purpose

### 1.1 Objective
This procedure describes how Meridian Supply Co. records and resolves supplier nonconformances and how repeated failures affect a supplier's standing.

### 1.2 Definitions
- NCR: nonconformance report, the record of goods or documents that do not meet specification.
- SCAR: supplier corrective action request, the formal request that a supplier investigate and fix the cause.
- QC hold: a controlled area where suspect stock is kept and cannot be picked.

## 2. Raising an NCR

### 2.1 Reporting deadline for an NCR
An NCR must be raised within 1 business day of the nonconformance being found, whether at receiving, in storage or after a customer complaint. The inspector records the PO, supplier, item, lot, quantity, defect description and photographs.

### 2.2 Quarantine in QC hold
All nonconforming stock is moved to QC hold immediately. It is tagged with the NCR number and is not released for sale or use without a Quality disposition.

### 2.3 Disposition
Quality decides whether the stock is returned to the supplier, reworked, scrapped or accepted under a documented concession. Damage found at the dock is first handled under WH-003.

## 3. Supplier Corrective Action

### 3.1 SCAR response time
Quality issues a SCAR to the supplier for every major NCR. The supplier must respond within 10 business days with containment, root cause and corrective actions. A late or inadequate response is itself recorded against the supplier.

### 3.2 Verification
Quality verifies that the corrective action works by checking the next three deliveries from the supplier. The SCAR is closed only after verification.

## 4. Supplier Performance Status

### 4.1 Probation trigger
A supplier that receives 3 NCRs in 6 months is placed on probation. The six months are counted back from the date of the latest NCR.

### 4.2 Effect of probation
While on probation, every delivery from the supplier is fully inspected, new POs need Procurement Manager sign-off whatever the value, and the supplier is told in writing what must improve.

### 4.3 Exit from probation
A supplier leaves probation after six months with no new NCR. A further NCR during probation is escalated to the Director of Operations, who may suspend the supplier or remove it from the Approved Supplier List.

### 4.4 Supplier quality measure
The supplier quality percentage is the share of units received in the period that were accepted without an NCR. It is reported on the Procurement dashboard and reviewed monthly.

## 5. Responsibilities

### 5.1 Receiving inspectors
Inspectors raise the NCR and move stock to QC hold.

### 5.2 Quality
Quality owns dispositions, SCARs, probation decisions and the monthly report.

### 5.3 Procurement
Procurement relays SCARs, chases responses and manages commercial consequences such as credit notes.

### 5.4 NCR categories
NCRs are classed as minor, major or critical. A minor NCR is cosmetic or documentation only. A major NCR affects fit, function or compliance. A critical NCR affects safety, and the affected lots are also traced to any stock already shipped to customers. Critical NCRs are reported to the Quality Manager the same day.

### 5.5 Records
NCR records, photographs, SCARs and dispositions are kept for seven years. The Quality team reviews open NCRs each week and chases any that have been open for more than 20 business days.

### 5.6 Cost recovery
Procurement seeks credit or replacement for nonconforming goods and may charge the supplier for sorting, rework or return freight where the supplier agreement allows.
